purpose: Routes that have been closed, with the reason each fails. A proposal that matches a closed lane must either cite new information that defeats the stated obstruction, or be rejected without spending a Lean build on it.

closure_kinds.circular: an exact identity that restates the target in other notation; proving it is proving the target
closure_kinds.lossy: the route is sound but discards more than the target can afford
closure_kinds.ceiling: the mechanism is real but its best case is provably weaker than the target
closure_kinds.refuted: the proposed target is not true at the stated scale, so no route to it can succeed

lanes.title: Bound the wheel residual by summing separately bounded square blocks
lanes.claim: Per-block bounds on Delta_j, summed, control the pinned wheel residual R_k.
lanes.obstruction: Only the signed sum telescopes. Replacing the signed consecutive sum by a sum of absolute block increments discards exactly the cancellation being sought and loses the scale required by the terminal target.
lanes.what_would_reopen: A theorem controlling the signed consecutive sum from independent arithmetic correlation information rather than through per-block absolute values.

lanes.title: Differentiate the square-root smooth and transport prefix decomposition
lanes.claim: Differencing the smooth-minus-transport prefix identity exposes a new cross-stage cancellation mechanism.
lanes.obstruction: The moving-cutoff reclassification term appears in both increments with the same sign and cancels identically, returning the original square-block increment. The derivative removes the moving-cutoff mechanism instead of exposing a new one.
lanes.what_would_reopen: Nothing at the level of the raw smooth and transport pair. A successor must retain additional lifetime, prime-fibre, or signed frontier structure.

lanes.title: Bound the survivor via residue energy and finite Cauchy-Schwarz
lanes.claim: Negative cross-cofactor covariance inside residue fibres offsets the diagonal strongly enough for an RH-scale survivor bound.
lanes.obstruction: The fibre split and prime-face toggle are governed by the same square-unit structure. Small moduli merely rebucket the survivor, while larger moduli make fibres more informative but pay the modulus factor in Cauchy-Schwarz. Far-upper rigidity further proves that a fixed-q prime-face fibre is exactly -M(floor(X_t/q)), so fixed-q pairing is a representation change rather than a complete cancellation mechanism.
lanes.what_would_reopen: A genuinely signed theorem acting across distinct prime fibres q, or pairing the survivor against another signed frontier before any norm is taken.

lanes.title: Use the single-prime c to 2c dyadic Li-residual pairing as the full RH mechanism
lanes.claim: Exact within-pair K and J cancellation, followed by random-like true-Mobius cancellation across cofactors and cleanup by the complementary main term and odd tail, yields the protected square-root bound.
lanes.obstruction: The exact within-pair cancellation is strong, but the aggregate system develops a slow coherent mode. The true Mobius signs can reinforce that mode, and full recombination with the complementary main term and odd tail does not provide a universal exact cancellation identity. The route is therefore closed as a standalone RH mechanism, while its exact dyadic identities remain available as local coordinates.
lanes.what_would_reopen: A genuinely new arithmetic mechanism that controls the coherent mode itself, especially a many-d or multi-prime signed theorem. Merely enlarging the finite range, reweighting the same single-prime pair, or taking another sign-blind norm does not reopen it.

lanes.title: Use the canonical absolute evolving-tail remainder state to realize cubic contraction at polynomial physical scale
lanes.claim: Self-compose the nonnegative one-log remainder, combine it with tail and small-quotient compensation, and obtain the cubic alpha^3 N log(N)^2 budget at a fixed polynomial cutoff in 1/alpha.
lanes.obstruction: NativePNTEvolvingTailObstruction proves a structural lower bound for the entire canonical evolving cost. The first absolute remainder contains the linear factorial defect, the second contains an N log N-scale floor, and the exact tail/small partition leaves at most alpha N log(N)^2 of negative compensation. At every fixed polynomial scale N = alpha^(-r), the N log N floor divided by the desired cubic alpha^3 N log(N)^2 budget diverges as alpha tends to zero.
lanes.what_would_reopen: Not by changing the cutoff exponent inside the same absolute state. A successor must keep additional signs before norms are taken. The current replacement is the signed second-Selberg square-stage ledger and signed prime-wheel frontier.

lanes.title: Bound the complete smooth mass as the square-root-scale residual
lanes.claim: The complete R-smooth Mobius mass A_R = sum over n < R^2 with P+(n) <= R of mu(n) satisfies |A_R| << R^(1+eps), so proving parity balance for the small-prime pool closes the argument.
lanes.obstruction: A_R is not the RH residual. Because X = R^2 - 1, every source below R^2 has at most one prime factor above R, so A_R = M(X) + T_R exactly and A_R carries the entire transport drift. The transport term contains a same-sign top block: every prime q in (X/2, X] contributes the single source m = q with mu(m) = -1, and that block equals its own cardinality with no internal cancellation. Parity determines the sign of a smooth squarefree source, but it yields nothing where the number of prime factors is constant. Only the orientation-split object A_R^born - T_R is at square-root scale.

evidence.numeric: measured growth of the complete smooth mass, the positive orientation, and the matched object over 100 <= R <= 2000

lanes.what_would_reopen: Nothing at the level of the complete smooth mass. A successor must keep the canonical orientation split, since the two orientations and their sum sit at different scales.

lanes.title: Transport the finite-prime CRT independence law onto the physical square-prefix population
lanes.claim: Identify the physical zero-free transition cells with the finite-prime CRT product law on complete aligned periods, leaving only a bounded square-clock boundary, and inherit the stationary Green-Kubo variance.
lanes.obstruction: Two independent ceilings. Geometrically, the square-block transition window admits the injection k -> 4k+1 into Icc(R^2, (R+1)^2) and so holds at most 2R+2 cells, while an aligned CRT period holds exactly the product of p^2 over the selected primes; complete periods therefore exist only when that product stays below the window width. Strict Walsh contraction needs p >= 11, and already {11,13,17} has period 5909761 and needs R >= 2954880, with the period growing doubly exponentially in the number of selected primes while the window grows linearly in R. Spectrally, the recombination terminates in the weight-one Walsh multiplier (q^2 - 2q - 4)/(q^2 - 6); its product over primes up to y is a Mertens product of order (log y)^(-2). A product of local multipliers of the form 1 - c/q cannot beat a power of a logarithm, so the interior supplies a polylogarithmic factor against a power target.

evidence.numeric: product of the weight-one Walsh multipliers over primes up to 10^7, matching 6.1/(log y)^2

lanes.what_would_reopen: A contraction that is not the local Walsh multiplier. Specifically a fixed factor below one per dyadic scale, which iterated over log R descents produces a power rather than a logarithm.

lanes.title: Bound the square-prefix endpoint by a weighted row-energy estimate for a lower-triangular operator
lanes.claim: Write the endpoint as a lower-triangular combination of lower-scale Mertens values and prove the weighted row-energy bound sum over y < R of (y+1)|a_R(y)|^2 at most A R; Cauchy-Schwarz against the lower envelope then gives the endpoint bound in one line.
lanes.obstruction: Cauchy-Schwarz is an identity at the optimum, so it supplies nothing. The least-norm solution of the single linear constraint has minimum row energy |E_R|^2 divided by the sum over y < R of |M(y)-1|^2/(y+1); since the envelope bounds that denominator by R K_R, the existence of any admissible coefficient vector is a statement at least as strong as the conclusion. The optimal coefficients are proportional to (M(y)-1)/(y+1) and so require the data being bounded. With the canonical arithmetic coefficients supplied by the prime-first transport transform, the row energy is dominated by the same-sign top fibre and grows like R^3 / log(R)^2.

evidence.numeric: row-energy scan for the canonical transport coefficients over 100 <= R <= 3000, measured log-log slope rising through 2.67, 2.71, 2.73

lanes.what_would_reopen: An arithmetically defined coefficient family whose row energy is near optimal, which would have to approximate (M(y)-1)/(y+1) without reference to the Mertens data.

not_closed.note: Several mechanisms remain intentionally distinct from the closed lanes. The direct centered square-wheel object H_{k,n} is still open. Signed cancellation across many reciprocal fibres or distinct prime-wheel faces is still open. The positive-orientation identity positiveSmooth(R) = -sum_{q<=R, q prime} M(q-1) is exact, but its observed large-scale envelope is diagnostic only and no asymptotic lower bound has been proved. The generalized affine PNT contraction is also live: the proved low-slope cubic step is alpha - alpha^3/178200000. What remains open is the physical cutoff law needed to realize repeated contraction at RH-compatible scale. The formal obstruction above applies to the canonical absolute evolving-tail state, not to every possible signed contraction architecture. Two successors remain explicitly live: a scale-descent contraction by a fixed factor per dyadic step, which is the only proposed mechanism whose success mode produces a power rather than a logarithm, and a global sign-reversing involution on factorization paths performed before absolute values, for which the same-sign top block is the sharp design constraint.
